Definition: of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor:--Mysia.
BiblicalUsage: Mysia is a region on the north-west edge of Asia Minor, and it shows up at a turning point in the mission to the Gentiles. Paul and his companions come to Mysia in Acts 16:7 and try to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit does not let them. They pass by Mysia in Acts 16:8 and go down to Troas, where the vision of the Macedonian man sends them into Europe.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Mysia teaches me to trust a closed door as much as an open one, for the Spirit who stopped Paul from going one way was the same Spirit who sent him another, and the gospel reached Europe because he listened. A no from God is still guidance.
